events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
The rider was charged a $6.61 cancellation fee on a trip the driver cancelled [F4][F7]. Under NS-0 the fee can only stand if one of the published branches is made out; here `cancelled_by = driver` and the driver's own statement is a rider no-show claim [F4][F12][NS-0], so the case is governed by NS-1 and its failure branch NS-2.

NS-1 requires all three of: (i) the driver pressed "I'm Here", (ii) GPS showed him at the pickup point at the moment of the tap, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting at the pickup after the tap [NS-1]. The first requirement fails outright on the record: the timeline shows `driver_pressed_here_at` is null, i.e. the button was never pressed [F6], and the driver himself admits he "forgot to press the I'm Here button" [F12]. The code trace marks NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) as ✗ for the same reason [F6][F1]. Because at least one of the three conditions is not fulfilled, the $6.61 cancellation fee may not be imposed on the rider [NS-2], and NS-2 directs a full refund.

I note the driver was in fact physically proximate — closest approach 33 m at 22:41:00 and 5 min 20 s cumulatively within 200 m before cancelling, with the last 4 minutes stationary 38 m away [F1][F2][F3][F5] — but geographical presence is not the NS-1 test: the policy's condition is the tap plus GPS confirmation at the moment of the tap, and the driver never tapped [F6][NS-1]. The driver's statement asserting he was there does not cure the missing tap, and under the system records rule the timeline and GPS control over the driver's statement [F6][F12]. This is not a case of a false "I'm Here" tap: since no tap occurred, the NS-2 flag_account trigger ("tapped I'm Here while not at pickup") is not activated [F6][F1][NS-2].

The amount is therefore the full cancellation fee recorded: $6.61, refundable as a voucher, this being a fee-waiver/refund claim filed by the rider [F7][NS-7]. Nothing in the traffic or weather facts bears on this branch — speed band 3 with no incidents and fair weather only indicate no external disruption, and in any event a driver-cancel case turns on NS-1/NS-2, not RD-4 [F13][F14][F15][NS-1]. The rider's own record (account age, rating, 0 disputes in 90 days) is consistent with the claim but decides nothing on its own [F16].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages — "At the pickup point, black Hyundai Ioniq." and "Waited 4 min, cancelling" — and the driver's written statement, plus the rider's complaint line "I was on my way down" [F9][F10][F12]. All are ordinary handshake/cancellation coordination with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the record is complete and every message is timestamped [F11]. The screen is none [SAFE-1]. No safety or evidence gap blocks the ruling: the two facts that decide it — the tap record and the timeline — are present and unambiguous [F6][F4].

You confirm you forgot to tap it, so the fee could not be charged. Being close to the pickup (about 33 m) doesn't replace the tap. No penalty or flag is being added to your account this time — just remember to tap "I'm Here" when you arrive.
